tin.account.name: Call it
tin.advice.nofiles: No CSV files in that folder. Tin reads the CSV export your bank offers, usually behind an Export or Download button next to your list of transactions.
tin.advice.notdata: Nothing in that folder is in a format Tin reads. It takes the CSV export your bank offers, or a TXT file laid out the same way.
tin.advice.pdfnothing: That PDF has no statement rows Tin could find. Either it is a scan, which holds a picture rather than text, or it is laid out in a way Tin does not recognise. A CSV export, if your bank offers one, is always the surer route.
tin.advice.pdfsigns: Tin found rows in that PDF but could not tell what went out from what came in. It looks for a minus sign, an S or H beside the amount, or separate debit and credit columns, and this statement has none of those.
tin.advice.unreadable: That file could not be opened at all. A PDF that is password protected has to be saved again without the password before anything can read it. A CSV export, if your bank offers one, avoids the question.
tin.chart.title: WHERE IT GOES
tin.column.name: Who it went to
tin.columns.title: Which column is which. Corrected once, remembered for every export with the same heading line.
tin.description: Reads the CSV exports your bank already hands out and says what is recurring, what quietly went up, and what is still going out for something you stopped using.
tin.dialog.folder: Which folder holds your bank exports
tin.empty: Nothing repeating found. Either the exports do not go back far enough, or a filter on the left is hiding everything. Three charges at a steady interval are needed before something counts as recurring.
tin.error.nofolder: {0} does not exist. Pick a folder.
tin.outlook.caveat: This is what the last few months did rather than a promise. Rhythms are counted at their own cadence, so a yearly premium counts once a year rather than a twelfth of it every month, and everything else is the middle month rather than the average, so one enormous month does not raise every month after it.
tin.outlook.madeof: {0} on a known rhythm, {1} in a typical month besides
tin.outlook.months: Worked out from {0} whole months. Part months at either end are left out of it.
tin.outlook.notenough: Not enough whole months to say what a typical one looks like. Two is the least it takes, and part months at either end do not count.
tin.outlook.short: More goes out than comes in at this rate.
tin.outlook.title: WHAT A MONTH USUALLY DOES
tin.problem.columns: Columns not recognised. Pick them below.
tin.problem.notdata: Not a format Tin reads. It takes CSV and TXT.
tin.problem.pdfnothing: No statement rows found in it. If it is a scan rather than a PDF the bank generated, there is no text in it to read.
tin.problem.pdfsigns: Rows found, but nothing said which were payments out and which were payments in.
